examples.name: ROS1 Talker
examples.expected: Guest exit0 after two successful publish calls; independent TCPROS observer checks at least one complete canonical hello String. Exact two-message quotas are measured separately by the bounded flood witnesses.

examples.name: ROS1 Listener
examples.expected: Guest exit0 after comparing all nine canonical String bytes and returned length; actual native TCPROS publisher is separate.

examples.name: ROS2 Talker
examples.expected: Guest exit0 after two successful publish calls; independent DDS observer checks at least one complete canonical hello String with compatible explicit reliable QoS. Publish success is not an exact native delivery-count proof.

examples.name: ROS2 Listener
examples.expected: Guest exit0 after full nine-byte reply/length comparison; native DDS writer is independent.

examples.name: ROS1 Service Client
examples.expected: Exactly one native Trigger request; Guest checks success1, length10 and complete hello response.

examples.name: ROS1 Service Server
examples.expected: Independent native client receives success1/hello; Guest uses its owned eight-byte request ticket and separate respond grant.

examples.name: ROS2 Service Client
examples.expected: Exactly one real native Trigger request and complete checked response; service request/response QoS is explicit.

examples.name: ROS2 Service Server
examples.expected: Independent DDS service client receives exact success1/hello, not a local mock response.

examples.name: ROS1 Parameter
examples.expected: Guest successful empty response; independent native parameter re-read sees exactly hello at /uwvm_resources/value.

examples.name: ROS2 Parameter
examples.expected: Independent selected native parameter node sees hello through the generated setter, with explicit service QoS and no remote declaration emulation.

examples.name: ROS1 Action
examples.expected: Actual Fibonacci order5 goal; checked owned-ID feedback and terminal [0,1,1,2,3,5]; repeated consumed result returns9.

examples.name: ROS2 Action
examples.expected: Actual UUID-backed Fibonacci goal/feedback/result; five separate native channel QoS contracts are explicit. This example does not itself prove all40 QoS fields.

examples.name: ROS1 TF
examples.expected: Real native TransformStamped base to map with exact frame names, translation1.25/2.5/3.75 and unit quaternion; Guest checks83-byte canonical response.

examples.name: ROS2 TF
examples.expected: Real native TF publication and bounded lookup, fixed frames/value limits; no implicit arbitrary-frame lookup permission.

examples.name: ROS1 Multi-Module
examples.expected: Actual camera_a/camera_b/controller/planner/hybrid functions; ROS1 Group sessions and quotas remain per Instance; foreign camera handle returns9 and unauthorized imports13.

examples.name: ROS2 Multi-Module
examples.expected: Same complete five-module run observes ROS2 planner/hybrid values; ROS1/ROS2/WASI Groups are separate authority domains.

examples.name: ROS1 and ROS2 Hybrid
examples.expected: Independent ROS1 publisher sends hello; Guest fully decodes/reconstructs String; independent ROS2 subscriber observes exact outgoing hello. No ros1_bridge or automatic version fallback.

examples.name: Unauthorized ROS1
examples.expected: A subscribe-only handle used for publish returns13; protected output remains unchanged and independent native publication/endpoint count stays0. Separate SDK absent rows test truly empty rights.

examples.name: Unauthorized ROS2
examples.expected: Operation substitution returns13 before actual DDS publisher creation or message effect, with unchanged sentinels.

examples.name: Cross-Module Capability Attack
examples.expected: Provider opens its own explicitly granted handle; main invokes provider.handle, then actual publish from the foreign Instance returns9 with no native publication.
